title: Task-Optimized Convolutional Recurrent Networks Align with Tactile Process

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The footnote says total sweeps equals the number of augmentation combinations × 9981 objects. Dataset (1) lists 316,192 total sweeps, but 316,192 is not divisible by 9981; 16 listed combinations would give 159,696, and 32 would give 319,392. Dataset (2) lists 2,076,048 total sweeps, which is 9981 × 208, but the listed factors (3 heights × 26 sampled values of speed/rotation/size) do not yield 208. The sweep totals are internally inconsistent with the stated object count and augmentation combinations.

predicted_errors.error_location: Appendix A4 (Inter-Animal Consistency) vs Fig. 4b caption
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Appendix A4 reports the maximum pooled animal consistency score as 1.34, while the Fig. 4b caption reports 'the maximum between all pairs of animals is 0.34.' A Pearson correlation cannot exceed 1 in magnitude, and the two stated maxima are irreconcilable without explanation.

Fig. 3 states 'Models with the encoder being S4 are excluded as the training losses explode before the first epoch is finished,' yet Section 4 compares neural fits against 'SSM-based (S4) encoder architectures' and Fig. 4b legend includes S4. Trained S4 models cannot be simultaneously excluded due to failed training and included in neural comparisons.

The equation defines \(\widetilde{\mathrm{RSA}}(X,Y) := \mathrm{Corr}(\mathrm{RDM}(x),\mathrm{RDM}(y))\) and then equates it to \(2\,\mathrm{RSA}(X,Y)/(1+\mathrm{RSA}(X,Y))\). The left-hand side as written is the raw correlation, whereas the right-hand side is the Spearman-Brown-corrected value; these are not equal.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, Model Training and Tactile Augmentations
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text says 'autoencoding (AE) [Olshausen and Field, 1996]' and cites Olshausen and Field 1996, 'Emergence of simple-cell receptive field properties by learning a sparse code for natural images.' That paper proposed sparse coding, not autoencoders; a correct autoencoding citation is needed.

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph on tactile sensor hardware
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The sentence 'prone to error from electromagnetic interference [Bhirangi et al., 2024b]' is supported by a reference titled 'Hierarchical state space models for continuous sequence-to-sequence modeling,' which is unrelated to magnetic tactile sensors or electromagnetic interference. The citation appears misattributed.

The abstract calls S4 and Mamba 'attention-based state-space models.' S4 is a structured state-space model with a convolutional representation, and Mamba is a selective state-space model, not an attention-based architecture. The Methods section itself describes Mamba via conv/SSM operations, not attention.

The paper claims the best models 'saturated all of the held-out explainable neural variance' and 'saturate our noise ceiling,' but no noise ceiling is computed or defined in Methods. The inter-animal 'a2a' score is a benchmark, not a noise ceiling, so the saturation claim is unsupported as stated.

Figure 5a legend lists 'SwAV' as an SSL loss, but Methods defines only SimCLR, SimSiam, and autoencoding as SSL losses, and the appendix model/training tables do not describe SwAV. The figure introduces a method absent from the rest of the paper.

The text states 'Specific learning rates, schedulers, and exact hardware scaling details are provided in Appendix A3 to ensure reproducibility,' but Table 3 lists only search ranges (e.g., SGD/Adam/AdamW and learning rates 10^{-1},10^{-2},10^{-3},10^{-4}) without identifying the exact optimizer/lr/scheduler used for each reported model. The reported results are therefore not exactly reproducible from the appendix.
